title: [Core] Make `ObjectDB::get_instance` lock-free

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Original PR: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118507

This improves multi-threading performance in all places that uses `ObjectDB::get_instance`. For GDScript VM it is mainly `Variant::get_validated_object` and `Variant::get_validated_object_with_check`. In exchange this will slow down object creation when it would need to allocate a new fixed size block.

I didn't write fixed for relevant issues because by itself this is this not fully fixes them, just improves multi-threading performance.

## What problem this PR fixes

All places that calls `ObjectDB::get_instance` share a spin lock, so it serves as a global multi-threading bottleneck. Debug builds are affected more severely because they use validated getter that uses `ObjectDB::get_instance` to check if it returns a correct object, release build is also affected to a lesser degree... Actually all [places](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agodotengine%2Fgodot+%22ObjectDB%3A%3Aget_instance%22&type=code) that uses it are affected, so I guess the performance impact could be more severe in a real project. I didn't test it outside of the GDScript VM itself.

## Technical overview

On master `ObjectDB` stores slots inside 1 array that it reallocates to a new one when it runs out of space with the new size multiplied by 2. This PR changes it to an array of 1024 blocks allocated in the setup once, with each block holding 16384 slots and allocated when `ObjectDB` runs out space, this approach allows us to not reallocate existing memory. The number of slots `ObjectDB` can hold overall didn't change, the speed of reusing existing free slots didn't change, but creating a large number of objects will be slower. Variables that are accessible from `ObjectDB::get_instance` were changed to `SafeNumeric` to make use of atomics.

This PR groups the data inside `ObjectSlot` into 2 separate atomics, the data itself and the pointer. By doing this we are making it possible to set and get each of them lock-free from multiple threads on all platforms. The `ObjectSlot` itself wasn't turned into atomic because the support for the 16-byte lock-free atomic is very spotty and inconsistent. With the data now being split into 2 atomics it rechecks the `validator` again after getting the pointer, by doing this we are preventing any possible data race with the `ObjectDB::remove_instance` and making sure we are getting the correct object.

To make the pointer atomic this PR introduces a new type `SafePointer<T>` that is a thin wrapper over `std::atomic<T *>`. It also adds a static assert about the atomic pointer being lock-free, the static assert was added after finding the usage of a atomic pointer type `std::atomic<SafeListNode *>` in `safe_list.h` and reading its design goals, mainly
> No blocking synchronization primitives will be used. 

And extrapolating from it that Godot 4 always assumes it is being used on platforms with lock-free atomic pointers. Because otherwise the atomic pointer usage will go against the stated design goal.

Now that I checked where `SafeList` is used it seems it already passes pointer types to `T`, for example `SafeList<AudioStreamPlaybackListNode *>` in `audio_server.h`, so it already asserts that pointer type is always lock-free with `static_assert(std::atomic<T>::is_always_lock_free);` with `T` itself being a pointer type. Adding the static assert to a new `SafePointer<T>` just makes it more explicit.

If maintainers deem the static assert unnecessary it can be removed.

All possible ways lock-free `get_instance` now works: 

1:
- Get: Passes slot data test.
- Get: Loads the object.
- Get: Passes the second slot data test.
- Get: Returns object.

2:
- Get: Doesn't pass slot data test.
- Get: Returns null.

3:
- Get: Passes slot data test.
- Remove: Other thread invalidates slot's data.
- Get: Loads the object.
- Remove: Other thread sets slot's object to nullptr.
- Get: Doesn't pass the second slot data test.
- Get: Returns null.

4:
- Get: Passes slot data test.
- Remove: Other thread invalidates slot's data.
- Remove: Other thread sets slot's object to nullptr.
- Get: Loads nullptr.
- Get: Doesn't pass the second slot data test.
- Get: Returns null.

5:
- Get: Passes slot data test.
- Remove: Other thread invalidates slot's data.
- Remove: Other thread sets slot's object to nullptr.
- Add: Other thread reuses freed slot, sets object.
- Get: Load newly set object.
- Get: Doesn't pass the second slot data test.
- Get: Returns null.

6:
- Get: Passes slot data test.
- Remove: Other thread invalidates slot's data.
- Remove: Other thread sets slot's object to nullptr.
- Add: Other thread reuses freed slot, sets object.
- Add: Other thread reuses freed slot, sets slot's data.
- Get: Doesn't pass the second slot data test.
- Get: Returns null.

The order of remove and add between each other is ensured by the spin lock, and the order of the commands inside of them is ensured by 
> In the new C++11 (formerly known as C++0x) atomic library standard, every non-relaxed atomic operation acts as a compiler barrier as well.
> https://preshing.com/20120625/memory-ordering-at-compile-time/

With both of them using acquire/release atomics, which prevents compiler reordering.

## VM Improvements

Places that always (not just on error) call `Variant::get_validated_object` and `Variant::get_validated_object_with_check` that are easily accessible from `gdscript_vm.cpp` that I could find

### Debug:
- `OPCODE_TYPE_TEST_NATIVE`
- `OPCODE_TYPE_TEST_SCRIPT`
- `OPCODE_GET_NAMED` leads to `Variant::get_named` with Object
- `OPCODE_SET_NAMED` leads to `Variant::set_named` with Object
- `OPCODE_GET_KEYED` leads to `VariantKeyedSetGetObject::get` (validated getter) with Object
- `OPCODE_SET_KEYED` leads to `VariantKeyedSetGetObject::set` (validated setter) with Object
- `OPCODE_ASSIGN_TYPED_NATIVE`
- `OPCODE_ASSIGN_TYPED_SCRIPT`
- `OPCODE_CAST_TO_BUILTIN` with Object
- `OPCODE_CAST_TO_NATIVE`
- `OPCODE_CAST_TO_SCRIPT`
- `OPCODE_CALL_ASYNC`
- `OPCODE_CALL_RETURN`
- `OPCODE_CALL`
- `OPCODE_CALL_METHOD_BIND`
- `OPCODE_CALL_METHOD_BIND_RET`
- `OPCODE_CALL_METHOD_BIND_VALIDATED_RETURN`
- `OPCODE_CALL_METHOD_BIND_VALIDATED_NO_RETURN`
- `OPCODE_RETURN_TYPED_NATIVE`
- `OPCODE_RETURN_TYPED_SCRIPT`
- `OPCODE_ITERATE_BEGIN_OBJECT`

### Release:
- `OPCODE_TYPE_TEST_NATIVE`
- `OPCODE_TYPE_TEST_SCRIPT`
- `OPCODE_GET_NAMED` leads to `Variant::get_named` with Object
- `OPCODE_SET_NAMED` leads to `Variant::set_named` with Object
- `OPCODE_GET_KEYED` leads to `VariantKeyedSetGetObject::get` (validated getter) with Object
- `OPCODE_SET_KEYED` leads to `VariantKeyedSetGetObject::set` (validated setter) with Object

## Performace testing (Outdated)

New test: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118803#issuecomment-4406289921

Build commands are the same as in the original PR. 
Test project: [testthreads4.6_target.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26926113/testthreads4.6_target.zip)

The basic test was to divide the iterations between threads and to perform the most basic interaction inside the loop, in theory this should imitate doing parallelizable work. The number of iterations was 200_000_000.

The results are presented as tables. In the columns was written the number of threads this attempt used, 0th thread is main thread that serves as the control.
Column type:
- `debug` - tested it in launched from Godot project
- `tool` - tested it inside tool script in editor
- `release` - tested it in export release

Tested on:
- EndeavourOS on X11 
- X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors 
- Vulkan (Forward+) 
- dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 (nvidia; 595.58.03) 
- Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9300H CPU @ 2.40GHz (8 threads) 
- 15.49 GiB memory

<details>
<summary>func_base, this one is fine, control</summary>
Setting values directly on the instance fields is also fine

```gdscript
func func_base(count: int) -> int:
    var time_before: int = Time.get_ticks_msec()
    var sum := 0
    for i in count:
        sum += 1
    finished.emit.call_deferred(Time.get_ticks_msec() - time_before)
    return sum
```

<summary>func_get, all affected</summary>

```gdscript
func func_get(count: int) -> int:
    var time_before: int = Time.get_ticks_msec()
    var sum := 0
    var obj := HelperObj.new()
    for i in count:
        sum += obj.increment # 'increment' is 1 
    obj.free()
    finished.emit.call_deferred(Time.get_ticks_msec() - time_before)
    return sum
```
